scope: Depleted close-assault admission through existing casualty-capable execution

reference.intent: Reference individual close engagement remains available independently of full-squad manoeuvre; preserve useful close response without creating a second movement owner.

finding: Assessment may select close assault for two or three armed infantry, and the shared drill executor already supports survivor pairs and three-person rebalance. AssaultStart still refused fewer than four actors and required two in each element. Fallback group reposition also lacked native PLANNING/protected-task deferral.
implementation: Two available armed actors can start the existing drill with one mover/one cover; three with two movers/one cover. No singleton scripted assault is inferred.
Small elements use armed non-leaders rather than requiring squad-only weapon-role distribution; native planning and protected tasks defer admission.

Larger group element requirements remain unchanged. Existing contact freshness/range, morale, hold-order, avenue, operation epoch/generation/lifetime, casualty replacement and physical progress still apply.
Routine reposition uses the existing shared actor-task/reservation boundary and native planning check before avenue work. Immediate close-armour withdrawal retains earlier survival priority.
geometryCost: No new geometry primitive or controller. Newly admitted small elements now use the existing bounded avenue selector; incremental runtime cost needs measurement.
remaining: Physical alternating pair movement, three-person swaps, casualty/recovery, fire-lane safety and native handback need verification.
Singleton outdoor engagement remains native; this is not complete parity with reference individual assault routing.
Normal/HC migration and performance budget remain unverified.

checkpoint.initialFinding: Existing indoor ownership test expected a direct reservation call. It now traces the shared task predicate into that same reservation boundary, retaining ordering before geometry/ownership and protected task checks.
